The following are the **scheduled events** of **association football** for the **calendar year 2022** throughout the world. This includes the following:

* In countries whose league seasons fall within a single calendar year, the **2022 season**.
* In countries which crown one champion in a season that spans two calendar years, the **2021–22 season**.
* In countries which split their league season into two championships, a system often known in Latin America as [Apertura and Clausura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apertura_and_Clausura "Apertura and Clausura"), all championships **awarded in calendar 2022**.

1. [↑](#cite_ref-2) League renamed from W-League after the 2020–21 season.
2. [↑](#cite_ref-3) In [A-League Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-League_Women "A-League Women") (as well as its male counterpart of [A-League Men](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-League_Men "A-League Men")), the term "champions" refers to the winner of the playoff tournament (known in Australian English as the "finals series") that follows the league season. The team that tops the league table is designated "premiers". This usage of "premiers" differs from other football codes in the country, which use that term to describe what the A-Leagues call "champions".
3. [↑](#cite_ref-4) Replaced the top level of the [Nadeshiko League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadeshiko_League "Nadeshiko League") as Japan's top league after the 2021 season. The Nadeshiko League now occupies the two levels below the WE League.
